## The economics of intelligence: speed vs. logic


Intelligence isn't priced as a monolithic commodity. The market has bifurcated into high-velocity pattern matching and high-cost logical deliberation.


> The bottleneck for AI performance has shifted from how much data a model has seen to how much compute it's allowed to consume during a single execution.


### The wide price gap in 2026 models


Modern API pricing reflects a massive divergence in the underlying compute required to produce a single token of output.


Docs highlights that while high-utility models like GPT-6 Luna cost only $0.05 per 1M tokens, making them nearly negligible for high-volume text classification, moving up to a reasoning-lite model like GPT-6.1 Sol jumps the cost to $2.00 per 1M input tokens, which means developers must carefully weigh performance gains against significant budget scaling.


A 22x increase demands a specific justification for the added logical overhead. At the frontier of logical discovery,[o3](https://modelpricing.ai/models/openai) sat at $2.00 per 1M tokens, a level that priced out all but the most mission-critical analytical tasks and made everyday experimentation prohibitively expensive at the time.


You must be certain that the complexity of the problem warrants a much higher price over the base tier, or you risk eroding your profit margins on simple queries, so every implementation decision must be weighed against its potential impact on your bottom line.


### Why logic depth costs more than standard generation


The price gap exists because reasoning models consume massive amounts of hidden thought tokens to verify their own internal logic before delivering a final answer.


### Hidden processing and billing for internal thoughts


A thought token is a discrete unit of computation used by the model to "think" through a problem before it commits to a final visible response.


Unlike output tokens, which you see in the chat window, these internal tokens are generated in a **hidden scratchpad** where the model tests hypotheses and checks for logical consistency.


Providers bill for these hidden tokens because they represent real GPU time and energy consumption during the inference phase. When a model spends a minute deliberating, it may generate thousands of internal thoughts for every one word of final text.


You are paying for the invisible work of self-correction, which is why a short answer from a reasoning model can occasionally cost more than a long essay from a standard one.


In a standard model like Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, the cost is low because the system predicts the next most likely word in a single pass.


> You are paying for the invisible work of self-correction, which is why a short answer from a reasoning model can occasionally cost more than a long essay from a standard one.


Running the work of ten standard queries to produce one verified result is how a model like Claude Fable 5.1 or GPT-6 Astra ensures a mathematical proof or a complex legal contract is sound.


### Calculating the 'reasoning premium' for enterprise tasks


To maintain margin, audit the workflows that are tied to your most expensive logic. Don't use expensive logic for cheap retrieval.


- For pattern-match tasks, use Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite or GPT-6 Luna for sentiment analysis or data extraction.
- For agentic workflows, deploy Claude Sonnet 5.5 or GPT-6.1 Sol for multi-step tasks like customer support routing.
- For logical discovery, reserve GPT-6 Astra or Gemini Deep Research for novel engineering problems or pharmaceutical simulations.
